title: What workflow/process is best for generating maps?
author: 88Y-J
selftext:
I've been trying to generate a fairly large map with different biomes and zones in Unreal Engine and was wondering what everyone else is using to do this.

Right now I've been feeding reference images into Claude Opus 5.5 and having it use Unreal's Landscape system to generate terrain based on those images. It's been working okay, but I'm not really getting the results I'm looking for.

Has anyone found a good workflow for creating larger maps with different biomes and terrain? Curious what tools or methods people have had success with.

  
I haven't been trying to do anything but topography so far.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
procedural generation lets you tune the generation

are you looking for spheres, cylinder worlds, rectangles, what?  planets, continents, regions, cities, one dungeon?

replies.author: 88Y-J
replies.body: Something like a pangea with different regions. Cities in some of the regions, plants, trees etc. Just was trying to do it in steps so topology first then adding plants, then buildings etc. Just wasnt sure if this was the best route.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body:
tell me about the map style

are we talking a big empty plane or are there hills?  is it continuous or divided into tiles?  etc
